source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 2.3, Proposition 2.2; reproduced and proved in Appendix A.5
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: For an interference network and contrastive effect, the paper states that for each q≥2 the design-based minimax risk is a function of the labeled conflict graph; its construction concerns the single specified model.

Theorem 3.1 states that minimax specification-testing error equals one for null and nested alternative exposure models at all non-trivial separation values; it is a testing result, not a squared-error global-effect estimator result.

The paper develops sharp partial-identification bounds for direct and spillover effects under misspecified exposure mappings and develops estimators for those bounds; it does not present a design-inclusive latent-menu minimax saddle.
The paper studies the all-treated-versus-none effect and derives a minimax rate over linear estimators and experimental designs under slowly decaying spillovers.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add a natural graph-local menu family, or a theorem showing why such a family cannot exhibit the persistent graph non-representability, to separate the substantive mechanism from the deliberately nonlocal common-selector witness.
Develop a bounded-degree or bounded-exposure-incidence compression theorem with an explicit algorithm, certificate size, and approximation ratio for the finite saddle.

Add Auerbach's rooted-network exposure-map framework as a comparator and state explicitly why its nested robust representation differs from a finite latent union with cross-model observation collisions.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0 with the exact finite saddle and persistent non-representability as the field-tier kernel; retain structural compression and natural graph-local separations as open extensions.
